Fortune Teller totals only support a yes/no on counts; names of visitors can't come from them. When a totals-only claim names visitors, treat it as either a fake or night-chat knowledge, and ask for the one result that only the real role could produce.

Your results are only two unordered totals. Never name who visited whom, even when public claims make the names seem to fit; a total that matches public claims is not a result, and naming identities is what got you distrusted.

Check your ballot against what you posted before the trial closes. Mismatches between stated stance and vote were the main case against Mallory, and an admitted slip costs trust even when the player is Good.

Before nominating, name the one checkable output (a result, token count, or group size) that would clear or convict the nominee. If nobody has one, hold the nomination; several Good players were hanged on pushes that had no such output.
Choose one role story early and keep it. Heidi's Neutral claim on Day 3, then Lookout under trial, then Arsonist, made a flip-flop the main case against her, even though the Arsonist story was true.
Spend one-shot tokens such as the Clerk rig on a decisive Day. Holding the token to the end wasted it and left the Village's late trials unaffected.

Compare each player's stated stance with their posted ballot before every trial vote and before pushing a nomination. Two Day 4-6 mismatches (a Guilty ballot posted as Innocent) sent Good players to the rope and became the hang reasons for the next Day.

A Fortune Teller only gets two unordered totals, so any claim that names who visited whom is either fake or night-chat knowledge. Treat named-visitor Fortune Teller claims as a Yakuza tell and test the totals against public visit groups before voting.

applies_to: Smuggler, Clerk and any Yakuza holding one-shot tokens
tip: Unused swap or rig tokens are wasted when the team is down to two or three players. Plan when a swap can redirect a live Vigilante shot or a decisive Day vote, and spend the token that Day rather than holding it for a Day that never comes.

Do not nominate a Good player on an unexplained visit right after a claim chain that checks out publicly. The late push looked coordinated and made the Clerk look like the one driving the hangs, so either add a second visible reason or stay quiet and let others carry the nomination.

Before accepting a claimed investigator's chain, check whether the claim names identities that its own result type cannot produce (e.g. a Fortune Teller naming visitors). Those slips are the cleanest Yakuza tells.
Never let a single living teammate become the only one pushing a nomination on a non-mechanical read; the town notices who pushes and who votes with them, and the pair becomes the case.
Check your posted stance against your actual ballot before every trial. Two ballot mismatches (Innocent posted, Guilty cast) cost a Good player a hang and gave a Yakuza-linked push cover.
Tie up the last living Yakuza early by pairing votes on a checkable target, since a 2-of-3 or 2-of-2 endgame lets the Yakuza pair hang the Village player who challenges them.

A Vigilante holding untouched shots should name a concrete trigger early in the game; holding shots silently through several Katana kills reads as either a Yakuza-protected claim or a fake, and it wastes the only kill-power left.

When a Yakuza flips, immediately list who voted No on their nomination or posted an Innocent lean, and make those players the default suspects for the rest of the game. Re-check them before every later nomination.
evidence: Frank and Judy were the only players besides Bob to vote No on Bob's D3 nomination, and Judy also posted 'voting Innocent for now'. Nobody raised this again. The Village instead hanged Ivan, Heidi and Mallory, and the two No voters won.

tip: Count how many wrong hangs you can afford before each Day. When one more mis-hang hands Evil the majority, nominate only from the remaining unconfirmed pool and never on a self-admitted slip by a player outside it.
evidence: On D6, 5 were alive with 2 Yakuza, and Dave was Oracle-confirmed, so Mallory correctly said the Yakuza were among Frank, Grace and Judy. Dave nominated Mallory over her ballot mismatches instead. That hang left 4 alive, the Katana took Grace, and the Yakuza held 2 of 3.

tip: Unused Vigilante tokens are lost Village value. Once several Katana kills have happened, fire a Basic shot on the best vote-based lead, such as players who protected a flipped Yakuza, rather than waiting for a perfect mechanical proof that may never come.
evidence: Grace held 3 tokens through five Katana kills and died on N6 with all of them. A Basic shot on Judy or Frank, the two No voters on Bob, would have hit a Yakuza either way.

tip: A fake investigative result must leave room for a killer other than you. Never claim a watch or track on the victim whose only other visitor cannot be the Katana holder. If a mapper or tracker might catch the holder, move the Katana or use a swap that night.
evidence: Bob claimed Lookout on Carol with Heidi, a declared Neutral, as the only other visitor. Everyone, including his own teammates, then pointed out that this made him the holder, and he was hanged 9-1. The Smuggler's 2 swap tokens and the option to pass the Katana went unused the night Alice, who had openly announced her map tokens, mapped Bob.

tip: Post your role and raw results early, and label clearly which parts are your result and which are deductions from public claims. Never call inferred information 'private'.
evidence: Ivan withheld his Fortune Teller numbers until D4, then said his 'private Night 2 information' showed who visited Carol and Alice. The Village read this as night-chat knowledge and hanged a true Fortune Teller whose numbers all checked out.

tip: Ignite once two or three living players are doused, or as soon as you are under suspicion. Pick one claim and keep it; every switch under trial makes you easier to hang.
evidence: Heidi doused Alice, Carol, Dave and Erin but never ignited. She went from 'Neutral' to Lookout to Arsonist and was hanged on D5 with zero kills, while Dave and Erin were still doused and alive.

tip: Double-check that your ballot matches the stance you just posted. As a voter, treat a mismatch as a lead to weigh against claims, not as proof.
evidence: Mallory posted Innocent on both Ivan and Heidi but voted Guilty both times. Dave and Grace used this as the main case to hang her on D6, and she was a Vanilla Villager.

tip: Bus a doomed teammate with Guilty votes, kill the information role most likely to expose you each night, and plan the endgame hang in night chat so you never need a token.
evidence: Frank's and Judy's Guilty votes on Bob were later cited by Dave, Erin and Grace to clear Judy on D5. The team killed Carol, Alice, Erin and Grace in turn. Judy laid out the D7 2-of-3 hang on N6 and kept her clerk token.

tip: Scout group results only rule links out for the groups named; a 'separate groups' result is strong evidence against visits among those three but says nothing about who visited a victim. Pair it with Fortune Teller counts and attack deaths to locate the holder instead of treating it as a clearance.

When a Katana kill happens, the living Yakuza holder must have visited the victim; list every player who could be the holder and check each against visit denials and skipped answers, rather than convicting on unnamed counts like 1/1 or 2/2.

Avoid unexplained Yes votes on Jester self-nominations and Village pushes; a Yes that helps a Jester win is read as Yakuza coordination, and it leaves a voting pattern that the town can check after the fact.
Do not let an untestable Oracle or Sheriff claim block every trial; ask the claimant for the visit behind the result and vote on the answer, since a stalled Day gives the Yakuza cover.

Check whether a claimed role is listed in the Yakuza section before accepting it, and remember that Fortune Teller and Scout numbers count holder visits too, so a Katana holder's own visit can make a count look like an extra visitor.

Watch the same target only once you know its exact role or suspicion is worth a night; a repeat watch on Judy showed only Grace, which was the single most useful public result, so plan a repeatable watch that confirms a holder before the Katana moves.
Before trusting a Fortune Teller or Scout count, enumerate every visit pairing that fits it; a 2/2 or 1/1 count names no visitor, so treat the number as a constraint on pairs, not as a name.
Do not let an untestable Oracle or Sheriff claim freeze every nomination; ask each claimant for the specific visit behind a result on Day 1-2, and vote the day a checkable answer is refused.

Yakuza with a living Katana holder should avoid long public stalls on checkable visits; the Village converged on the Katana holder through visit denials and skipped-night answers, so answer visit questions yes or no cleanly.
When a player's private messages to a suspect appear in the public PM log, expect that suspect's Day votes to be read against those PMs; decide early whether to explain PMs or stay silent.

An Oracle guess is astral and only confirmed to its user, so publish the guess as a checkable claim only with a full night-by-night record; state early that the moderator's private result is the only proof, and never assert the moderator confirmed it to the table.

Build a visit-count table each night (Fortune Teller 2/2 vs Lookout/Tracker visits) and test every visit claim against it; a 1/1 or 2/2 count that names no one is strong evidence only when combined with a named visit that must be consistent with it.

A Katana kill needs a living holder who visits the target; if the Village has a Fortune Teller and a Scout, avoid giving them extra visits (Diviner, Fabricator, Lookout-type checks) on the same night the Katana acts, since every extra link shows up in their numbers.
Do not let one untestable claim (Oracle, Sheriff, Diviner) decide several trials; list each vote's reason and check it against verified results before supporting or blocking a nomination.

A Jester or Executioner pushing for a hang on an accused player is most credible when they repeat the push publicly with checkable reasons; the table reads repeated self-nominations as a win-seeking tell, so vary the reasoning or accept the suspicion.

Test every exact-role or astral claim against which visits and deaths it implies; a Katana kill proves a living holder visited the victim, so check each claimant's own visit denials against that night's group and count results.

Do not let a Jester's self-nomination pleas or a trial's outcome be the only test; when one player repeatedly pushes a hang, ask what they privately discussed and whether their nominations served a possible Jester win before voting with them.

Map the Fortune Teller's two numbers against all known visits each night rather than trusting a single count; ambiguous 1/1 or 2/2 results name no visitor, so use them to rule links out, not to convict.
Spread visible claims and votes so no one player's Yes or Innocent pattern looks like coordination; a teammate who repeatedly votes with a Jester on hang pushes draws the table's attention.
Remember a Katana holder can use their own role action the same night, so a double visit by one player is legal and should not be treated as a contradiction on its own.

Don't spend three nominations on one suspect whose only evidence is a single visit claim; check visit counts (Fortune Teller, Scout groups) against every other claim before voting, because a flat count with no names can't convict anyone alone.

Keep votes consistent with stated reads: Ivan's repeated Yes votes on Jester-aligned nominations and his 'I won't repeat it' followed by another Yes gave the town a concrete, unanswerable contradiction that got him hanged.

Answer direct visit questions with a plain yes or no the first time; dodging a single question (like Night 5) across several Days was treated as guilt, and the same dodge on Night 3 and 4 is what made Heidi's trial.

A Katana attack is a visit by the holder, so a visit-based result on a dead victim (Lookout or Scout) can prove the holder; track who was alive and held the Katana each night rather than arguing over unverified Oracle or Sheriff claims.

Assume every Village player reads night chat-style visit patterns; the holder who alternated visits and denials ended up with the living Village lead to chase, so keep visit answers uniform across all teammates.

Test every claim against the visit-based results that can actually be checked (Lookout watches, Scout groups, Fortune Teller numbers) and against the seating; exact-role claims like Oracle cannot be checked by any visit, so don't let them decide trials.

A Fortune Teller's 1/1 or 2/2 counts name no visitor; before trusting them, check whether the FT's own visit (or a self-visit) could be the one counted, and ask each suspect directly whether they visited on that specific night.

When a player repeatedly self-nominates or pushes a hang, check whether the hang would win for them (Jester or Executioner after the target died) before voting; a Jester who wants the hanging is often the loudest voice.

Keep the Katana holder's visits minimal and avoid giving a Lookout or Tracker a second visitor to a victim; the Lookout's single watch on the target exposed the holder, so vary which players are watched and never leave one visitor alone at the victim.

Do not send teammates private messages on Day 2 or Day 4 about nominations or trials; the Village reads PM triangles, and Dave's and Judy's PMs to Ivan and Grace made the table distrust the very players who were trying to help the team.

Avoid a Katana kill on a Village player who is still a live threat only if the holder is already exposed; otherwise a visit-based Lookout watch on the target lets the village reconstruct the holder from one death. Rotate targets so the only other visitor is never the holder's own role action.

Do not let a teammate's Day-1 PM or nomination pattern become the only defense of a Yakuza. Vote with the team on trials even when it looks risky, because abstaining from a Guilty vote on a pushed nominee made Innocent votes look like coordinated protection.

Before a claimed role's group result is tested, check whether your own night actions are public. A Diviner claim whose groups fit the seating is easy to defend; a Diviner claim alongside a Katana visit on the same night was the contradiction the village used. Keep your claimed role's visit count consistent with the Katana visit or drop the claim.

Count visits from Fortune Teller numbers against every visit claim before trusting any role. A 1/1 or 2/2 count with no names constrains many claims at once; list the possible visit pairs explicitly on the day numbers post.

Ask a suspect for a yes-or-no answer to one checkable visit question early, and vote on the non-answer if it persists; repeated dodging of a visit question was the most useful signal in the late game.

Never claim no visits when a count or Scout group could contradict it. My flat no-visit denials on Nights 3 and 4 were false, and Mallory's 2/2 and 1/1 counts plus Erin's pressing turned them into the case against me. Agree a plausible cover visit with teammates, or say less.

A Katana attack on the target of an active Lookout watch exposes the holder. Bob's Night 2 watch on Judy showed Grace as her only other visitor, and his will later revealed it. Before striking a watched player, check whether a Lookout is alive and watching them, and prefer killing the watcher first.

applies_to: Yakuza with a one-shot token (Clerk, Puppeteer, Mortician)
tip: Spend the one-shot token on a decisive Day, not in reserve. I held my Clerk token through six Days and died with it unused, which gave the Village a free trial and left nothing to swing a vote.

If an Executioner's target dies to a Katana rather than hanging, the Executioner becomes a Jester whose win needs a hanging. Hanging such a player hands them the win, so treat repeated self-nominations from them as a reason to refuse the vote.

Test each night's counts against the visits they imply. Fortune Teller totals, Lookout watches and Scout groups together constrained the Katana holder to a few players each night, and that cross-checking is what exposed the Yakuza here.

A Katana holder who visits the target also shows up in a Lookout's watch and in Fortune Teller counts; rotating the holder to a teammate who had no other visits kept the Katana team from being linked, but I (Ivan) never took a visit and was still the living holder candidate by elimination. Keep a visit-free holder rotation and avoid giving the Village a living candidate pool of only two or three players.

Refusing to answer yes/no visit questions and then nominating a teammate-adjacent player looked worse than any single visit would have. Answer visit questions directly and early, even with a truthful 'no'; repeated dodging became the Village's case against Heidi and then against me.

Private messages to village players (like Judy's PM asking me to vote Yes) were visible as a PM event to everyone and later became the case against me. Do not PM village players from a Yakuza seat during the Day, and do not let a Jester teammate-adjacent Village player use PMs to steer your votes.
Voting Yes on a self-nomination after saying you won't repeat it looked like a Yakuza bloc signal; once you commit a stance in public, change it only with a stated reason posted before the vote.

Fortune Teller 1/1 or 2/2 counts with an unnamed visitor cannot identify the holder; the village spent several Days arguing about who visited rather than checking whether the count itself could include the FT's own visit. Ask the FT directly whether their own action was a visit before treating the count as evidence against a specific player.

A Jester whose own vote cannot end the game safely should still post a concrete, checkable reason to the table; repeated self-nomination offers with no evidence were read as a Yakuza-style push and drew no votes, so the win never came.

Track the Katana holder by visit groups and Fortune Teller counts rather than by claims: a Katana kill requires the holder to visit the victim, so the living player who can be the visitor shrinks each night and should be tested against every denial.

Before nominating a player on a checkable Night result, ask the table to name the exact visit pair the claim needs; several Village players hung on unverified exact-role claims or on votes that merely echoed a Jester's offers.
Keep private day messages to a minimum and never PM a Jester or a likely nominee about the vote; Dave's and Judy's PM trails were the main reason the town grouped Ivan and Grace together.
Expose your pushes publicly and stop repeating the same self-nomination; a third identical offer read as a wish to be hanged and lost credibility with the table.

Keep a per-night table of your 2/2 or 1/1 counts and test every public visit claim against them; a count that fits only one combination of visits is the strongest checkable evidence in a game where Scouts and Lookouts are dead.
Do not let an untestable exact-role claim (Oracle, Diviner) steer trials; demand the visit behind any claim before voting, because the claimant can be a Yakuza feeding false roles to block tests.
Track which players PM a likely Jester or a dying target, and ask them what the PM said before each vote; private contacts were the main unexplained pattern this game.
Once a Katana holder is suspected, collectively list the living players who could have visited each night and clear them by visit evidence, rather than hanging on vote patterns alone.

A Katana attack is a visit by its holder, and a holder may also use their role; so a dead target with one other visitor implies that visitor is the holder, but a Yakuza who holds the Katana may also act visibly, which gives false cover.

When one player is openly begging to be hanged, spend an exact-role check on them early and claim the result as soon as a hang of them becomes possible. A confirmed Jester read shuts down the Jester's (and Executioner's) win and frees the table to hunt Yakuza.
evidence: Carol guessed Judy = Jester on Night 1 and claimed it on Day 2. Every later nomination of Judy, and of Dave after he became a Jester, failed. Her Night 2 and Night 3 guesses (Dave Executioner, Bob Lookout) were also correct, which made the rest of her claims credible.

tip: Treat Fortune Teller counts as hard constraints. Add up the claimed visits each night and check them against the two numbers. When the count is 1/1 on a Katana-kill night, the only visitor is the holder, so anyone whose claims would add a visit is lying. Then demand a yes/no denial for each specific night from every remaining candidate.
evidence: Night 1's 2/2 fit Bob's watch plus Grace's divine, leaving no room for Judy's claimed visit to Ivan. Nights 4 and 5 at 1/1 narrowed the holder to a few players. Heidi denied Nights 3 and 4 but skipped Night 5, which led to her hanging and the Village win.

tip: Never fake-claim a role that exists only in the Yakuza section of the role list. It is a self-confirming tell. If you're cornered by a visit result, claim a Village role whose visit pattern fits what was seen.
evidence: Grace claimed Diviner at her trial. Erin and Frank both cited 'Diviner is a Yakuza role' as a concrete reason to vote Guilty, and she was hanged 7-3.

tip: Before choosing a Katana target, check whether a Lookout or Tracker has publicly said whom they will watch. Kill someone else, or kill the watcher first, rather than walking into a watched player.
evidence: On Day 2 Bob announced 'I'll watch Judy again on N2'. Grace still hit Judy with the Katana that night, Bob saw her, and she was hanged the next Day.

tip: Keep your vote record clean. Bus a doomed teammate, never vote to hang a known Jester, and don't break a public promise about your votes. Spend your one-shot tokens (rig, frame) before you're cornered; unused tokens die with you.
evidence: Heidi voted Guilty on Grace and lasted to the final Day. Ivan voted Innocent on Grace, then voted Yes on Jester Dave's self-nomination on Day 5 after saying he wouldn't, and was hanged for it. Heidi died holding her clerk token, and Ivan never used his frame.

tip: An investigator claim with an Evil read on a specific player paints a night-kill target on you, especially if the read happens to be true, and a Jester killed at night wins nothing. Fake claims that invite a hang without threatening the Yakuza work better. Once you've been exact-role outed, repeated self-nominations just burn budget.
evidence: Judy's 'Sheriff: Ivan Evil' was accidentally correct, so the Yakuza Katana-killed her on Night 2. Dave nominated himself seven times after Carol outed him and never got more than 2 Yes votes.

tip: Spending a prosecutor token on a Day-ending trial only matters if the target can't dodge it; the target is announced at the start of the next Day, so a Yakuza can plan a Katana kill on the prosecutor the same night. Prosecute only when your own survival is secured or the trial's outcome is decisive.

Track the Yakuza slot math from the archive and the Diviner/Tracker results every night; a confirmed Yakuza role (Diviner, Pharmacist, Grunt) counted against the living list identifies who must be Yakuza far earlier than trial votes do.

Self-nominations by a player who has already confessed a lie are often a Jester pattern, but a Jester hanged is a win, so the Village should weigh that before letting a confessed liar keep pushing votes; hanging the Jester early can be fatal.
Early Village votes on confirmed-Evil suspects were split by unverifiable claims; agree on which claims are testable (visit results) and vote only on those, rather than on who pushed hardest.
A Katana holder appears Good to alignment checks that night, so Seer/Sheriff contradictions can be explained by the holder rather than by a liar; check holder timing before treating a split as proof.

A Katana holder who also has a passive or visit-based role should keep the Katana on a low-value member and avoid repeat targets that expose the holder through Tracker visits; in this game the Yakuza kept a holder who was publicly visible through repeated Tracker results.
Keep a stable, checkable cover story for your nightly action (e.g. a Grunt with no action) and never make a daytime push that depends on a claim you cannot defend under vote.

Submit the agreed Katana target every night even when a teammate is blocked or dead; a lone remaining Yakuza with no backup should prefer targets whose role can't expose them, since Village can still trial by pure votes.

A confessed-invented claim plus repeated self-nominations can be a Jester hunting the hang; a Village player should weigh a Jester's win condition before voting Guilty on a self-nomination, since a hanged Jester wins outright.
Use the archive slot math and visit results together: an Ex-Con always shows a visit unless blocked, so a 'random visit' claim can be checked against Tracker and Lookout results.

Keep the Katana holder's visit list separate from your role's visits: a Tracker who sees the holder visit the target learns the team's kill, and a Diviner pick on a Tracker lets that Tracker see your own visits. Choose the holder and the Diviner pick so a single track cannot tie them together.

A false Sheriff or Seer claim that is later confessed collapses the claimant's credibility and gives the Village a clean case. Use a fake claim only when the real claimant's results can be contradicted by the Village's own night results.

A single investigative result that one player posts is weaker than a result corroborated by another source; when two claims conflict, ask which one a Good player could produce without a visible contradiction, and hang only on mechanical checks.

Self-nominations repeated after a confessed lie look like a Jester seeking the hang; a hanged Jester wins outright, so Village should not vote Guilty on them without a mechanical reason, and Yakuza should not rely on them to end the game.

Before Day 1 each night, agree the Katana holder and target in night chat and confirm all votes; a block on a dangerous Oracle or Tracker should be decided the same night so that the Pharmacist and holder do not choose different targets.

Post a single fully verifiable result early and claim it with its visit list; investigators who hid results until Day 3 lost the chance to corroborate each other while Yakuza kept killing them one per night. Holding info back mostly helped the Katana holder pick off the most informative players.

Day 1 'no claims, wait for results' stalemates handed the Yakuza free nights; agree on a rule like 'every investigator posts a result by Day 2 or is treated as a suspect', and have each investigator name a planned tonight-target privately before the night so their results can be cross-checked.

Track the role census against claims early. Grace's archive plus the revealed claims showed two Yakuza roles among the survivors, and the Village that counted slots could have targeted those two earlier instead of pushing Mallory or self-nominating Frank, whose repeated nominations drained Day time.

Don't trade your vote on a single confessed-invented claim alone; a self-nominating confessed liar can be a Jester hunting a hang, but a Yakuza who confesses a fake Sheriff can also be trying to get a Good player hanged. Pair the read with a mechanical check before voting, and remember that hanging Good voters is what loses the game.

Keep the Katana holder alive and out of public claims; a Yakuza who flips a Day 2 trial with an invented Sheriff claim, then survives by staying quiet, can win the endgame with the Katana repeatedly killing Village investigators at night.

An Ex-Con's random visit is never reported to the Ex-Con, so it gives no information; claim it only if you need a cover for reading Evil, and expect the table to test it against visit results. Post a checkable Ex-Con read early rather than late, because a claim that reads Evil next to a confirmed Evil Carol invites the Sheriff-style suspicion that I could not refute.

Track which living player is a confirmed Katana holder by watching who votes on the Katana and who the Yakuza night summaries name; a Yakuza that holds the Katana rarely needs a second visible action, so a player who never visits and never claims is a strong Yakuza candidate.

When a Pharmacist-style block lands on an investigator, check who was blocked on each night against who later died to Katana; repeated blocks on the same Village roles are a Yakuza signature and should be weighed before any Party Animal claim is trusted.

Do not let a single confessed-false claim lead to a long run of self-nominated trials; a self-nominating Jester can force hangs, and a Guilty vote on a Jester who wants the hang wins the game for them, so require a checkable result before voting Guilty on any self-nominee.

Keep the Katana holder and target agreement visible in night chat, and avoid letting one remaining Yakuza take the Katana alone at the end when only two Yakuza remain; a single living holder with a fixed night routine is easy to read from the death pattern.

A Jester who wants the hang should self-nominate sparingly and make it look like a mistake; repeated self-nominations after a confessed lie get read as a Jester pattern and draw Innocent votes from everyone, so the win fails. Spread the pressure through other players' nominations instead.
Track who voted Yes on a nomination with no stated basis, then ask them to name the checkable result behind it before the trial, not after; the unanswered question decides the vote.

Use the archive slot count early and keep it updated with every death and revealed alignment; the game turned on whether Pharmacist and Grunt could be placed, and I never converted that into a concrete suspect list.
Treat a role-block on a Good investigator as a Pharmacist or Party Animal signal and post it early, because it points at the blocker's team before any trial.
Keep the Katana holder's night chat concise and agree the holder before the target; the team lost its holder to executions only twice, so holder continuity mattered more than target choice.

Spend the archive token only when the roster is small enough to cross-check; a 7-of-10 role list with no names mostly helps the Village if you can match it against confirmed claims early, so announce the list the moment you get it and ask claimants to confirm the roles they hold.

Track which claims are mechanically checkable in the next night and which are pure words; a self-nominating player who repeatedly invites Guilty votes is a Jester pattern, so do not let that alone drive an execution when only two or three players remain.

When Yakuza night chats are visible through patterns (same target chosen, same blocks, same Katana holder), count the Katana holder as the most dangerous player and check whether a Tracker or Lookout can cover them before the holder moves.

A track result showing a visit to a player who then dies to the Katana is strong evidence, but check whether the visitor was a Diviner/role-blocked pick before treating it as proof; ask the visitor to name the unchosen targets of their own claimed actions.
Avoid pairing a claimed Good role with self-nominations that invite Guilty votes; a repeated self-nomination after a confessed lie reads as a Jester and let the Village ignore the real Yakuza.
Keep a running slot count from the archive or survey and update it after each death; once the Yakuza role list is accounted for, it narrows the suspects fast.
Do not let a Guilty vote on a single unverified check decide a hang when few players remain; with three or four living players, one wrong hang can end the game for the Village.
Post the track result immediately rather than holding it for a planned day, since a Yakuza with a Pharmacist can block the Tracker and the result is most valuable before the next night.

Before spending a night on a repeat block or kill, check whether the target's role is already known or announced; my Pharmacist blocks on Mallory and the Katana on Mallory were predictable and told the town where the Yakuza were looking.

Never let the team become the only voting bloc on a trial that matters. Our Day 6 Guilty vote on Ivan and Day 7 Innocent votes meant that when the Village flipped on us, we had no living ally, so keep a plausible non-teammate to vote with for cover.

A fake claim that contradicts a living player's public result (here, Frank's Sheriff read on the Oracle) gets tested immediately; if you must fake, pick a role whose results the table cannot check against a reliable visit or token count.

When a player's claim and a visit-based result disagree, weigh the mechanical result more heavily, but also check whether the visitor's own role could have been role-blocked that night, since blocks can make a Good visitor look silent.
Repeated one-line self-nominations and identical 'no new result' posts spent budget without changing votes; use nominations sparingly so they stay a real signal.

A Seer pair result that conflicts with a claim should be tested against visits and the Katana holder's alignment-hiding before being posted; a single unverified split was the only lever the table had on Carol, and the Yakuza exploited the Katana appearing Good to muddy it.

Track the Katana holder explicitly each night: a holder appears Good to alignment checks, so any Seer or Sheriff split from the holder's night is unreliable, and the holder may move to a new Yakuza after a death.

Repeated self-nominations after a confessed lie are not evidence either way; vote on checkable visits and results, and do not let a self-nominating player steer the hang when the Jester revenge risk is real.

Teammates who keep the same night target and Katana holder for many nights create a visible pattern; vary your Katana-holder and target choices and avoid pushing Guilty on town claimants without a mechanical reason.

Ask early for every role's night results to be posted in a fixed order, and whenever a claimant is attacked, note exactly which claim was attacked; this makes the Yakuza's blocks and attacks readable as a pattern.
A role-block on a Good Oracle is ambiguous. Track which living players could hold Pharmacist or Party Animal, and test blocks against visit reports before reading them as proof of a Yakuza.
Count Yakuza slots from the archive and the Katana holder's visits, not from claims. Self-nominations and confessed lies alone do not show who is Yakuza; a Jester hunting the hang looks the same.
Set up a night-by-night checklist of which claims are still unverified and which visits they predict. Nominate on contradictions that a single result can expose, instead of pushing bloc votes.
Before voting on a bloc that backs one nomination, ask which member has a checkable result. Voting in lockstep with an unverified leader gave the Yakuza easy cover.

Katana holders appear Good to alignment checks, and the holder can change each night. A Seer or Sheriff read of a Yakuza player can be wrong for exactly the night that matters, so weigh it against visits.

Don't form an isolated Guilty bloc on a Village claimant's trial. If your teammates are the only Guilty votes, the vote record becomes the town's list of your team once any one of you flips. Vote with the majority unless your votes can actually decide the trial.
evidence: On Day 2 the Guilty votes on Mallory were exactly Bob, Carol and Ivan, and the trial failed 3-7. After Carol flipped Evil, Alice and Erin pressed Bob and Ivan over that vote every day, and it led Alice to prosecute both of them.

applies_to: Yakuza Katana holder with a visiting role
tip: If the Katana holder also uses a visiting action, a single track shows two destinations, and the second one is the kill. Either pass the Katana to a Grunt or other non-visiting teammate, or skip the holder's own action on kill nights.
evidence: On Night 2 Carol divined Heidi while killing Judy with the Katana. Heidi tracked Carol, saw both visits, and Carol could explain only the Heidi visit. She was hanged 8-1 on Day 3.

tip: Never claim your real Yakuza role. Prepare a Village cover claim, plus a cover reason for any visit that might have been seen, before you hold back results, because sitting on unposted results draws suspicion.
evidence: Carol hinted for two days that she held a Night 1 result but would not post it, then claimed Diviner. Erin, Grace and Mallory immediately pointed out that Diviner is a Yakuza role a Good player cannot hold.

tip: Spend Day-forcing or one-shot tokens as soon as a solid lead exists, while enough Village are alive to win the vote. Holding them until the endgame lets the Katana remove your voters first, and you may die with the token unused.
evidence: Alice had a strong lead on Bob and Ivan by Day 4 but first prosecuted on Night 5. Ivan's hanging came only after Grace and Mallory were dead. Her Night 6 prosecution of Bob came to trial on Day 7 after Alice had been killed, and it failed 1-2. Judy likewise kept her Seer token 'for a stronger night' and died with it.

tip: Aim guesses at the top suspects, using the roles still unaccounted for on a public list. Don't spend them on a player whose behaviour already marks him as a likely Jester.
evidence: With Grace's archive leaving Pharmacist and Grunt unaccounted for among Bob, Frank and Ivan, Mallory guessed 'Frank = Pharmacist' on both Nights 4 and 5. Frank had confessed a fake claim and self-nominated over and over, the typical Jester pattern. 'Bob = Grunt' or 'Ivan = Pharmacist' would have been right.

tip: In a three-player endgame of Yakuza, Village and Jester, the Jester's vote decides every trial, and hanging the Jester never helps the Village. Village must make the Yakuza hang the only goal and win the Jester's vote. Yakuza can buy that vote by promising the Jester a future hang.
evidence: On Day 7 Bob privately promised Frank a Guilty vote on Frank's next self-nomination. Frank voted Innocent on Bob, saving him. Erin then voted Guilty on Frank, giving the Jester his win, and Bob killed Erin that night.

tip: A fake investigative claim that you later confess, followed by constant self-nominations, marks you as a Jester, and the table will refuse to hang you for days. A better plan is to look plausibly Yakuza and save your push for the endgame, when your vote has leverage.
evidence: Frank's fake Sheriff claim and its confession, followed by more than seven self-nominations, were rejected again and again: the trials went 4-6 and 1-9, and later nominations got only 1-3 Yes votes. He won only because the Day 7 endgame gave him the deciding vote.

tip: Protect the player most likely to be a Katana target, but rotate who you protect so a Yakuza can't predict your protection; a self-protect costs a token, so keep one spare for a late-game duel.

Treat a Fortune Teller's unlabelled numbers as a constraint to test against known visit records, not as proof; the holder's visit set was ambiguous for several nights and the Village chased one suspect too long.

Before nominating or voting Guilty, ask whether the target's own claims and results contradict each other; behaviour patterns (late answers, pushing trials) are weak reasons to hang and cost the Village Vanillas.
Watch for a bloc that votes identically on every nomination for several Days; when three players march together, a concrete mismatch in one of them is the best lead to press.
Count the living Yakuza and the stall rule early: a Yakuza team that has lost its kill-capable members can only win by a kill on schedule, so track Katana holders and their visit sets nightly.

Once you hold slot information the Yakuza want, expect a Katana on you that same night. Post the list and its slot math in your first public speech and keep your will current, because my public Day 2 claim made me the Night 2 target.

Before using a Fortune Teller count or a Lookout watch to name a holder, list every visit the table knows (a Lookout's watch is itself a visit, and a Veteran's alert kill is a visit) and check whether the count forces a unique visitor. A count that leaves five candidates should not drive a nomination.

A bloc that votes identically across several nominations and then pushes a nominee on one wording slip is itself a lead. Vote on the bloc's own concrete points, and do not hang a Vanilla on a wording mismatch that the accused has already explained.

Never claim a Yakuza role name, even by slip. Erin's Grunt claim was caught by the public archive list and gave the Village its first hard contradiction. Pick a Village role that fits the slot math and check every repeated claim against the list.
Days 1 and 2 filled with 'no nomination from me' and 'agree with X' posts that cost budget and gave no information. Spend budget on one concrete question or result per turn instead.

While a Fortune Teller lives, each Katana visit shows up as an unnamed extra visitor in the counts. Plan the holder's visit to coincide with a visit the town already counts, or remove the Fortune Teller before the Katana hits, so the count can't narrow the holder to your team.

Village players will hang each other on thin behaviour reads. Let them nominate and vote on those reads, and keep your votes on the record consistent with what you said, so no one can use a mismatch against you.
Answer direct questions about night visits plainly and early. A late or evasive answer after a nomination looks worse than a direct one, and days of pressure follow silence.

Before each night, agree on one holder, one target, and any rig or swap in night chat, and have every living member confirm. This kept the Katana plan in sync for six nights and avoided any cancelled kill.

Going on alert with a token is only a kill if someone visits you; spend alert tokens when a Katana holder is likely to strike you, and report visit counts publicly so the town can cross-check Lookouts and Fortune Tellers.

A Fortune Teller's unlabelled numbers can be matched against Lookout watches and Veteran alert counts; test each number against known visits before treating it as evidence, and don't let a dead investigator's unverified counts drive a hanging.

Vote on mechanical results and concrete contradictions only; a bloc that voted together every trial since Day 5 was the strongest pattern, and pressing a single Guilty-then-Innocent wording slip repeatedly wasted several trials.
Deny visits only when no result could expose you; a Katana holder who repeatedly denied visits and was checked by Heidi's counts became the target of trials, so keep an honest cover story ready.
Late silence on a direct yes-or-no visit question reads as guilt; answer plainly early, because dodging until nominated was the main behaviour lead against Grace and it carried into the trial.

Before a Katana attack, check whether the target has an active alert or Medic protection that night; a Veteran on alert kills any visitor, so attacking a Veteran's visitor-free night is safe but Standard beats only None-defense targets, so aim at players with no protection.

Keep the Katana holder unchanged and move the attack target only after agreeing in night chat; the holder who keeps repeating the same role and visiting the same kills gets read by Fortune Tellers and Lookouts.
Vote as a bloc only when the bloc's votes look independent; Carol, Erin and Mallory voting identically on every nomination from Day 5 onward gave the Village an obvious pattern to follow.
A dead teammate's claimed role never needs defending; deny visits plainly and early, since Heidi's count forced repeated public denials that became the case against the group.

Count visits from Fortune Teller numbers against Lookout and alert results before hanging anyone; visit-count deductions are fragile when a dead holder's claim is unverified, and a Village player who keeps pressing trials on thin reads is often just a Vanilla who has misread the situation.

Audit results only show a token total at the end of the night, so an audit on a player who spends a token that night looks lower than their starting count; compare audits on the same player across nights and remember that Heidi's count and audits can both be wrong if a visit is misread.

When a Fortune Teller's numbers and a Lookout's watch disagree, check whether the Lookout's own visit was counted in the visitor total before accusing anyone; much of the Day 3-4 debate came from that mix-up.
Ask for plain yes/no answers on specific night visits early, and treat a denial that is only given after a nomination as weaker than one given on the first ask.
Do not let a bloc of players vote identically on every nomination go unnoticed; record which players voted together and test whether their stated reasons are concrete before following them.
Keep public messages short and specific once the budget is tight; late in the game long repetitive messages cost budget without adding new mechanical information.

Track voting blocs from the first nomination. When three players vote identically on every nomination (No together, then Yes together), treat them as a unit and test that unit against night results before the Village splits. I noticed the Carol, Erin and Mallory pattern only after Day 5.

applies_to: Village (Fortune Teller, Lookout and other visit-count roles)
tip: Enumerate every visit each night and check which living players could fill any unexplained visitor slot. A count that needs one unseen visitor is a puzzle to solve, not a lie to hunt; denials from players who visited nobody don't narrow it.

Don't publish nightly targets and numeric results in public while the Katana holder is alive. Heidi's Night 2 and 3 counts and Judy's public watches named visit sets that the Yakuza could plan around, and Heidi was then killed by the Katana on Night 4.

Don't keep the Katana with the same member all game. Erin held it from Night 1 to Night 6, which gave the Village one fixed suspect to chase. Rotate the Katana to a low-value member with a cover story, and move it on the night a visit-count result would name the holder.

A claimed Veteran on alert kills every visitor, so a visit to a real Veteran is a death and not just a missed result. Village players should avoid visiting claimed Veterans at night, and Yakuza should treat any alert Veteran as a hazard to the holder, not only a target.

Post your visit-count numbers with explicit visitor names as soon as they land and keep them consistent; unlabelled counts plus a Lookout watch left the table unable to pin the fourth visitor, and I died before the count could be tested.

Treat a single unexplained slip (like a wrong role claim) as weak; the Village hanged on behaviour reads (late answers, nominations) while the Yakuza bloc of Carol, Erin and Mallory voted identically from Day 5 and won by voting together.

When several Village players share a suspicion, split who nominates and who votes so a bloc cannot exploit a single trial; Ivan and Grace pushing trials on each other let the Yakuza bloc win the numbers.
Track who votes identically across every nomination; a three-player bloc that votes as one is itself the mechanical lead, and it should be named with the vote record early.

Visitor-count claims are only as strong as the counted visits; when a Veteran alert kill is publicly confirmed, the visitor list it produces is a hard fact that should anchor every count checked after it.

A mismatch the player has already explained once is not a fresh lead. Carol's Guilty-then-Innocent point was renominated three times across two Days, and my own renomination on it preceded my execution. Require a new fact before each renomination.

Name a bloc early when its members vote identically on every nomination and trial for a day or more, and ask each member the same concrete question in public. Carol, Erin and Mallory voted as one unit from Day 5 and won the endgame.

The Katana holder killed the Archivist, Accountant, Fortune Teller and Veteran by Night 5. Post results publicly as soon as they are safe, and give Fortune Teller counts with each visitor named, since an unnamed count could not be tested after she died.

Visit-count results (Fortune Teller numbers, Lookout watches) cannot name a Katana visitor. Use a count as a test only when each visitor is named, and do not nominate on a suspect list derived from a bare count.

One Katana holder who never moves the Katana, with teammates voting the same nightly target, was the trio's strongest engine. Aim each kill at whoever holds the most information, and let the holder stay low-profile in public.

A Lookout's watch only reveals visits to the watched player, so a clean watch on a Yakuza suspect rules out nothing about that suspect's own nightly visits; use watches on likely Katana targets or on players who claim to be Veteran-adjacent instead of on quiet players.

Check a Fortune Teller's numbers against visit records before building cases on them; the numbers only fit a visit set and several sets often fit, so treat them as a constraint on counts rather than names.
Vote on a single target every night with a clearly stated holder; repeated 'ready' confirmations in night chat cost nothing but reveal the team's pattern to any Eavesdropper or post-game reader.

A trial pushed by one player before facts are in invites a bloc response; if you nominate, state the specific mechanical result you need, since behaviour-only nominations lead to lynches of Village players.

Stated votes that contradict posted intent (e.g. 'I vote Guilty' then Innocent) are a readable tell; either vote as you say or explain the change before the reveal, because the town will use the mismatch as a lead.

Once the Katana holder is known and the Village has a visible Veteran or Fortune Teller, count visitors before picking a target: a Fortune Teller's two numbers can expose a Katana visit, so kill the Fortune Teller early rather than letting their count name your visits.

When a Village player asks a plain yes-or-no visit question, answer immediately and plainly, and avoid any answer that can be checked against a visit count later; a late or dodged answer became the main lead against our own teammate-adjacent players.

Keep your voting pattern on nominations varied, for example one Yakuza votes No on an early nomination of a teammate-adjacent Village player, otherwise a three-member bloc that votes identically every time is visible to everyone and draws a bloc accusation.

A Veteran's alert kills show exactly who visited them, so a Veteran's alert counts plus the Katana's kill list pin the holder's visits; compare each Katana victim's death against every visit claim before trusting any Fortune Teller number.

Do not nominate a player on a wording or typo slip that the player has already explained; the same slip repeated in later votes was used to justify a chain of nominations and lost the Village its last Vanilla players.

A player who claims a Yakuza role and only retracts it after being called out is the strongest lead you will get. This is especially true when a public archive confirms that role exists and nobody else claims it. Hang them while the Village still has the numbers. Don't let 'it was a typo, show me a mechanical result' talk you out of it.
evidence: Erin claimed 'Grunt (Village)' on Day 2 and Bob's archive listed one Grunt. Her trial still went 2 Guilty to 7 Innocent. Grace (the nominator), Ivan, Judy and Dave flipped to Innocent after Mallory and Carol argued a slip isn't a result. Erin held the Katana for every kill.

tip: Veteran: don't announce your alert nights publicly. The announcement only scares off the Yakuza, who visit by choice, while Medics and Lookouts still walk in. Everyone else: never visit a player who may be on alert. Treat a claimed Veteran as off-limits for protection and watches.
evidence: Dave announced alerts on Day 2 and Day 4. In night chat the Yakuza said 'nobody visits Dave' every night. His only kills were Alice protecting him on Night 2 and Judy watching him on Night 4, both Village.

tip: Record every nomination vote. A group that votes No together to save the same suspect is a likely Yakuza bloc. Push that bloc right away, while the Village still outnumbers it, not once parity arrives.
evidence: Carol, Mallory and Erin were the only No votes on Erin's Day 3 nomination. The Village only named this bloc on Days 5 and 6. By then the same trio could block Ivan's Carol nomination 3-3 and then hang Ivan 3-2.

tip: Vote the way you said you would, or explain the switch publicly before the vote. Treat other players' unexplained read/vote mismatches as leads worth pressing.
evidence: Several Village players said Guilty on Erin and voted Innocent, which saved the Katana holder. Carol said 'Guilty on Grace' on Day 3 and Day 6 but voted Innocent both times. That was a real tell, and Ivan and Grace correctly chased it.

tip: Don't spend budget on repeated filler like 'no nomination from me, wait for results'. Save it for the late rounds, when you will have to answer direct questions and argue at trials. Answer a direct question in your very next turn, in one short line.
evidence: On Day 3 Heidi couldn't afford a public answer to 'did you visit Bob?' and looked evasive. On Day 5 Grace and Mallory were locked out of public speech by round 7. Grace's slow answer to the Night 2 visit question nearly got her (a Vanilla) hanged 4-5.

tip: Use a Clerk rig on a Day when the Village is already piling onto an innocent player, because any passing nomination then becomes a free execution. The Village usually builds those nominations itself after a confusing night.
evidence: Grace's Day 3 nomination passed 8-1 and her trial failed by one vote. A rig would have hanged a Vanilla without cost. Mallory sat on her token all game, and Carol never used her 2 swaps.

tip: Fortune Teller: line your two numbers up against every claimed visit, publicly and early. Then ask everyone without a night action to deny the leftover visit by name. Remember that Lookout watches and Accountant audits count as visits.
evidence: Heidi's Night 2 counts of 3 and 4 correctly showed one hidden visitor on Bob, the Katana holder. She first said a Lookout watch wasn't a visit and had to be corrected, which slowed the analysis. Erin's flat denial was never matched against Judy's watch on her and her Grunt slip.

tip: Do not sit on a limited token for days waiting for consensus; if a town-wide lead never forms, a Prosecutor's tokens are wasted once blocked or killed, so spend one on the most credible suspect once a contradiction appears.

Track which players have never stated a role. Silence on role claims for several Days, especially from a player in a Pharmacist-compatible group, is a concrete lead to press early rather than after a Katana streak.

Vote on evidence the whole table can verify. Pushing a hang on a single dead player's claim (Carol's group) led to executing a Good player while the Katana kept striking, so prefer hangs backed by a live contradiction.

Avoid private messages to teammates or pleading for a Jester's hang in daytime PMs; Wiretap/Eavesdropper-style reads and PM triangles make coordinated voting visible and the Village will read them as a bloc.

Check whether a claimed Diviner group or a Seer pair is consistent with circle positions and living players at the start of the night before accepting or rejecting it; a clean circle check is decisive evidence.

Never let a Katana holder who is also the last Yakuza sit silent for multiple Days; Frank's Jester pressure and my own silence on role claims made Grace's Night 8 nomination look justified, and a survivor who refuses to state a role gets hanged. Post a plain role claim early (Grunt) and keep it consistent.

Avoid private messages to Village-aligned players during the Day when a Wiretap or Eavesdropper could be active; Frank's private DMs to Bob and Erin on Day 6 and my own DMs to Frank on Day 8 became public-facing evidence the Village used to read the table.

When a teammate has been hanged and only you remain, a Jester survivor can be an ally only briefly; spend the last Days making the Village target Village-aligned players whose claims conflict with results, rather than arguing for an outright self-nomination pattern that draws suspicion.

Track which town claims conflict with the circle geometry and archive slot count before voting; the circle check on Frank's Diviner group exposed him fast and was the cleanest mechanical lead of the game.

When a player's Guilty vote is followed by a self-nomination loop, the Jester revenge and hanged-Jester win make a blanket Innocent vote on that Jester too risky; confirm the Jester read with a result before any trial.

A Diviner's group of three should be checked against the circle before claiming it: a pick on a player draws that player's living neighbours, so an impossible group (like Frank's Mallory/Ivan/Bob) exposes a liar fast. As Yakuza, avoid claiming a role whose group or result can be cross-checked by a living Tracker or circle-aware player.

Visiting a target with your Katana leaves a Tracker trail. Pick Katana strikes so the holder's visit is not also the Diviner or other action of the same night, or make sure the holder's own role action is not revealed as an extra visit, since a Tracker's exact track on the holder's night is the decisive evidence against you.

Do not let a teammate publicly defend a player they nominate or vote Innocent on in ways that are only explained by alignment; Bob's repeated Innocent votes and private messages to the Jester Frank were noticed and used as a case against him. Keep Innocent votes tied to a public, checkable reason.

Late in the game, long repeated self-nominations and identical push messages cost budget and gave no new information; spend budget on specific contradictions and results instead, since repeated lines were ignored by the whole table.

A Jester who keeps self-nominating can be killed off by being left alone; when the Jester is the only one pushing a hang, voting Innocent costs little, but a dead Jester-hunt is a real win condition for them, so check whether the nominee is a Jester before the revenge risk matters.

A Lookout watch that comes back with nobody visiting can still be a blocked watch or a Katana-holder's cover; log watches as 'visitors none' only when the block result was absent, and prefer watching the player whose Katana-visit status is in question over a player already cleared.

Before trusting a Diviner or Tracker group, check the circle: a claimed group only works if its members were neighbours at the start of the night, so run the circle check on every such claim immediately.

When only one Yakuza remains and holds the Katana, the Village should pick a single nominee early each Day and vote together, because split Yes votes on different players let the holder strike a claimed role each night.
Do not let a self-nominating Jester's pleas decide votes; a Jester who is hanged wins, so separate a Jester's Guilty-pushes from genuine contradictions before each trial.

Track which roles are Yakuza-only (Diviner, Grunt, Pharmacist) and remember that a self-claim of a Yakuza role by a Village player is a strong lie signal, but a dead player's claim is never verified, so do not build a hang on it.

Your random visit is never revealed to you, so a visit-based result on you is uninformative; when the Yakuza are hunting Village roles, your own clean night can't be used to prove anything, so spend effort on claims and votes instead.

Treat a dead teammate's pre-death claim as untested unless a visit or result on a living player confirms it; a Katana strike on a claimed investigator is evidence of a Yakuza visit only if the visit itself is verified.

Before nominating or voting, ask who gains from a living Jester hanging versus who gains from a living Yakuza surviving; a Jester who self-nominates repeatedly and asks for Guilty votes should be hanged only with a concrete contradiction, since a hanged Jester wins outright.

Watch private message patterns on Day: several PMs to one player asking for the same vote before a trial is a strong bloc signal, and PM requests for Yes votes from a player who was just nominated are worth reporting publicly to the town.

A Katana strike is a visit by the holder to the target; Yakuza with a Night 2 visit to a living Seer who is then killed should be checked against the Tracker's track before trusting any single Diviner claim.

Before trusting a Tracker or Lookout trace, check it against the circle: a Diviner's group must match the living neighbours at the start of the night. Frank's fake Diviner group failed this check and exposed him, so verify group claims mechanically rather than by trust.

With one Yakuza left, do not PM the Village or push a self-nominated Jester toward a Guilty vote that can revenge-kill a living voter; keep your teammate-free plan private and avoid repeated private pleas that the Eavesdropper or Wiretap can read.

Do not let one suspicious pattern (repeated self-nominations) substitute for a concrete contradiction. A Jester who wants a hang can look identical to a liar, so require a mechanical lead before voting Guilty, and watch who keeps the trial alive with private lobbying.

Your self-nominations only matter if others vote Yes; a Jester who admits the lie and repeatedly asks for a hang gets pushed to No, so pick a single credible route to the hang early rather than spamming nominations that wear down your speaking budget.

A dead Yakuza-claimed role (like Diviner) or a dead Ex-Con's random visit cannot be verified; a Katana holder's Night visit is the only lead, so compare Katana-visit tracks to the exact target and the holder's own claimed actions.

Spend the archive token on a night where the role list can be cross-checked against claims; my 7-of-10 list was useful only once several claims were already public, so consider holding it until more players have committed.

Track the Katana holder across nights: a Katana attack is a visit by the holder, so a Tracker's visit trace on the kill night is the strongest lead, and a Yakuza who keeps the Katana through late nights is usually the last one standing.

When a self-nominating player says they are a Jester, do not let their pushes decide votes; instead insist the group name a concrete contradiction, since a hanged Jester wins and cheap Guilty votes hand them the game.

Once only two Yakuza remain, a Village pair that keeps voting Innocent together can deadlock the trial; split votes on a player with a real contradiction rather than repeating the same nomination that already failed.
A false role claim that fails a mechanical check (like a circle-neighbour test) is fatal; pick a claim whose group the town cannot check, or keep the claim vague.

A Tracker's result of an investigated player visiting a Katana target is the only evidence of the Katana's source; ask the holder to explain their visits before the vote, since a Katana strike always needs a visit by the holder to the target.
Night chat plans that say 'Ivan blocks X so the visit fails' leak information when the blocker's own actions are public; avoid repeating the same block pattern night after night.

Self-nominations by a player who claims no role are a Jester pattern and cost the town days; when a Jester is possible, hold a vote on a concrete contradiction rather than repeated silence-based trials.
Consistently vote holder and target with the teammate and avoid PM-ing the teammate publicly-observable patterns; a Yakuza who claims Grunt with no explanation of nights draws suspicion.
Check the circle when a Diviner or Tracker group is claimed: dead and alive neighbours change each night, so a group that skips a living neighbour exposes a false claim.

Before a Pharmacist or Katana team member role-blocks, check the moderator's visit logs; my Night 2 block on Dave (a Lookout) was announced publicly by others, so blocking the same watch-holder repeatedly drew suspicion that a Pharmacist was active.

When only two Yakuza remain, avoid patterns that reveal the team (same block target on consecutive nights, Katana holder switching with no reason); vary blocks and keep the holder stable only when necessary.

Do not reveal your role by speaking in specific night-plan terms in public, and avoid claiming to be an unclaimed role that the archive slots make obvious; a silent Pharmacist who refuses to state role for many Days becomes the top nominee.

Track which players are pushing repeated self-nominations and private vote requests; those patterns are cheap-to-test information and a Jester can use them to force a hang, so note them early in the notepad.

Use archive or survey slot math early and write each dead player's claim-consistency into a notepad line so that later contradictions (like a Diviner claim covering two nights of visits) are caught quickly.

Spend the Seer's chosen-pair token early, when it can be compared against a second result, rather than saving it for a late test; my last token on Carol and Heidi returned 'same alignment' and died before anyone could use it.

When a Katana holder is possibly active, a claim that conflicts with a visit log (e.g. a Diviner pick count vs. a tracked double visit) is strong evidence; weigh the tracker's exact result above the accused player's own explanation.

Late in the game, a lone surviving Yakuza with a Katana should avoid Innocent votes that look like protection of a Jester-claimer; the town flagged the pattern of defending one suspect while repeatedly self-nominating partners survived.

Don't rely on a single unverifiable role claim's 'Good' statement; ask players to answer the same concrete question and vote on the consistency of their answers, since a refusal to state a role for several Days was the strongest read on Ivan.

Remember that Jester wins by being hanged and that the revenge kills a Guilty voter; a repeatedly self-nominating player with no night role should be treated as a possible Jester win condition, not as a clear Yakuza.

Guessing an exact role on a living player is a cheap, testable check, but a guess on a player who is a Yakuza or key Village role can be blocked; spread guesses across suspects so a single Pharmacist block doesn't waste your only testable lead each night.

Track the Katana by visits: a holder who kills a Seer or Tracker-visible target usually shows up in a Tracker or Lookout trace on that night, so compare who visited each kill rather than trusting a claimed Diviner group.

Don't let a single unverified claim (a dead Diviner's group, a dead Tracker trace) decide a hang; in this game two Village players were hanged or nearly hanged on dead-role evidence while the real Yakuza kept voting Innocent to protect the last teammate.

With two Yakuza alive, the Katana holder and target must match; spend Day PMs carefully since Erin and Wiretap-style readers can see them, and avoid pairing a Yakuza's Innocent vote on a Jester-like player with a visible protective pattern.
Self-nominations by a probable Jester are a cheap way to force a hang, but a hanged Jester wins outright; treat repeated self-noms as a Jester tell and weigh the risk before voting Guilty.

When the Katana kills an information role every night, 'wait for next night's results' is a losing plan. Each Day you skip costs a Village life and probably the result you were waiting for. Once a player is the best mechanical fit (named by slot math, fits observed blocks, and refuses to claim a role), hang them that Day.
evidence: From Day 4 on, Grace, Dave, Erin, Mallory and Alice all named Ivan as the likely Pharmacist: Carol's Night 1 group drew a Pharmacist, Dave was blocked on Night 2, and Ivan never claimed. Yet everyone said 'no nomination before Night 4/5/6 results'. Dave, Mallory and Alice died in that time. Ivan was hanged only on Day 7, and by then the endgame was lost.

tip: Spend Prosecutor tokens on your best mechanical read before the Yakuza kill or block you. A prosecution guarantees a trial without needing a majority to nominate, so it beats endless nomination requests. Unused tokens at death are pure waste.
evidence: Alice claimed Prosecutor on Day 4 with 2 tokens. She kept 'holding them for a lead the Village agrees on' while she herself named Ivan. Ivan blocked her on Nights 5 and 6, and Bob killed her on Night 6 with both tokens unspent.

tip: Don't leave the Katana with a member who also uses a visiting night action. The holder's kill plus their own action shows as two visits, which a Tracker reads as proof. Give the Katana to a Grunt or another member with no action, so there is only one visit to explain.
evidence: Carol held the Katana and also divined Grace on Night 2. Heidi's track showed 'Carol visited Grace and Judy', and Carol could not explain the Judy visit. Once the Katana passed to Bob (Grunt), he made five unexposed kills.

tip: Never claim your real role if it is a Yakuza role, and never switch from a bare 'I'm Good' to an Evil role claim. If you're caught visiting, have a Village cover role agreed in night chat beforehand, with a story for each of your visits.
evidence: On Day 2 Carol said 'I'm Good' twice. On Day 3 she claimed Diviner. Dave, Erin and the rest immediately pointed out that it is a Yakuza role and can't explain two visits, and she was hanged 8-2.

tip: Check any claimed group result against the circle (dead players removed) and against the public archive list. A fake group with the wrong neighbors exposes a liar at once.
evidence: Frank claimed a Diviner Night 3 group of Mallory/Ivan/Bob. Grace pointed out that Mallory's living neighbors were Ivan and Alice. Frank had to retract and admit he lied. Grace's archive slot math also correctly placed Pharmacist and Grunt among Bob, Frank and Ivan.

tip: Speak only from public information. Saying a dead player was Yakuza in a no-reveal game is a slip the town will catch.
evidence: On Day 7 Bob said Carol's claims came from 'a player we now know was Yakuza'. Erin immediately noted that roles are never revealed, and Grace used the line as her Guilty reason against Bob on Day 8.

tip: Constant self-nominations and begging for Guilty votes make the town refuse to hang you. Build suspicion indirectly with a plausible Village claim and believable mistakes. In a final three with one Yakuza, remember you lose if the game ends with you alive, so plan your hang before the player count gets that low.
evidence: Frank self-nominated more than 15 times. Every trial on him ended Innocent because players cited 'Jester hunting a hang'. On Day 8, Bob reminded him that hanging Bob would end the game with Frank alive. Frank kept Bob alive and still lost.

tip: Record each night's planned target in your will before the night, labelled as a plan. If you die that night, your result is lost, but the plan still points the town at your suspect.
evidence: On Night 5 Mallory correctly guessed Ivan = Pharmacist, but died that same night. Her will had no Night 5 plan, so the confirmation never reached the town. Dave's will even said 'Night 4 target: undecided'.

tip: Treat a visit result as evidence of who went where, not proof of what action they performed or what result they received. State that limitation clearly, and combine visits with independent claims and later flips.
A partial, partly fake role sample is not a role census. Before using an information result to accuse someone, check exactly what was sampled and what conclusions the mechanics permit.

Keep a public vote ledger. After a Yakuza flips, revisit who opposed the nomination or voted Innocent, but treat those votes as leads whose timing and likely vote math still matter—not automatic proof.

Use hard facts about the current state to test claims. For example, a known Katana kill proves a Yakuza was alive when that night resolved; compare that with claims about who would remain after an execution.
When a claimed Jester may win by hanging, avoid giving them that outcome just to test a claim. Prefer tests that preserve the Village's options, and hang only when the evidence justifies the risk.

Choose the Katana holder strategically each night. The holder appears Good to alignment checks, so if a Sheriff is likely to check a teammate, consider giving that teammate the Katana for that night rather than leaving it with the same person by default.

Treat swap tokens as a way to disrupt a key night, not just a last resort. Coordinate the swap with the Katana plan and likely investigations, while accounting for the fact that all actions targeting either swapped player—including the Katana attack—are redirected.

Avoid endgame statements that imply private certainty about the remaining factions. Make faction-count arguments explicitly conditional; a confident claim about who would remain after a lynch can reveal that you know your own teammate is the last Yakuza.

applies_to: Archivist and anyone using sampled role lists or counts
tip: Before using a partial sample (like an Archivist list of 5 real of 7 players) to cap or count roles, check the sampling rules. It only limits what was sampled. I built a public accusation on a 'one Vanilla slot' misreading, had to retract it, and it cost the Village a day of credibility.

Don't vote Innocent on every nominee to stall. Three straight unanimous Innocent trials burned the Day and pushed the game toward the R14 stall rule. Name a concrete test or nomination early in the Day, and keep a running clock on how many quiet Nights and Days remain.

applies_to: Village claimed info roles (Archivist, Sheriff, Lookout, Medic)
tip: Publicly claimed info roles get Katana-hit fast. Carol, Alice and Heidi were all attacked after claiming or being checked. Medic protection was the only defense, so stagger public claims where possible and make sure a protector is ready to cover the most exposed claimant each night.

Stalling with unanimous Innocent votes and Jester-plea defenses looked suspicious when Village reads Yakuza from voting patterns. If you must defend a teammate, do it with specific counterclaims and avoid repeating the same protective line across several trials.

Check whether a result's source is a visit or a result before treating it as proof. Alice's watch showed visitors, which only confirmed a visit, not what the visitor learned, and Frank's protection of Heidi was a visit to Heidi, not Frank. Keep visit evidence and result evidence separate in your reasoning.
A partial sample caps nothing. An Archivist list covering 5 of 7 others does not mean there is only one Vanilla in the game. Count role slots only when the list covers every living player.

Check claims against night outcomes. A Katana kill on a claimed Village role makes protection or survival claims testable. A bare Not Evil on a Katana holder clears nobody, so weight Evil results more heavily than Not Evil results.

With a claimed Jester alive, don't stall the Day on the Jester claim. Set a concrete test, such as an Evil result or a corroborated visit, and vote once it lands, because the stall rule (R14) can end the game for everyone.
Avoid conditional end-game arguments like 'if I'm executed, the rest are Village'. They reveal that you know the team count and read as a tell. Explain a bad vote directly instead.
Repeating 'still Vanilla, no new info' every turn burns budget at rising round multipliers without changing votes. Spend budget on one specific question or result per round.
Keep endgame arguments separate from hidden faction-count assumptions. Even a conditional claim like “if you execute me, everyone left is Village” can imply you know who the remaining Yakuza is.
Use public claims to update the kill plan. Once a Medic has publicly claimed and described protections, consider removing or blocking them before they protect more important targets.

After a flip, revisit earlier votes in context: a teammate’s Innocent vote may become a useful lead, but check whether that vote could actually have affected the outcome before treating it as strong evidence.

Once claimed, self-protect (Standard, 1 token) on nights you are exposed, and rotate protection instead of covering the same claimed investigator every night. The Katana killed the unprotected Medic on Night 4 while two tokens sat unused.
Publicly confirm that protection happened without naming the target. Naming protected players each Day tells the Yakuza which claimed investigator is safe, so they hit the rest.

An archive or survey that samples only some players cannot cap how many of a role exist. Do not build duplicate-liar arguments on slot counts from a partial sample; it wasted two trials here before the retraction.

Watch the R14 stall count across Nights and Days. A quiet Day can end the game for everyone, so when deaths stop, push for a real test (a result or a nomination) early instead of waiting for the last Day.

Before voting Guilty on a single uncorroborated Sheriff result about a claimed Vanilla, ask what independent check could confirm it. A lone result is a lead, and I hanged on it before any second source existed.
Don't trade your vote on a shaky narrative. Day 5's Erin trial shows a single Innocent vote can flip the outcome; before voting Innocent on someone, ask whether the evidence actually clears them.

A Jester who openly claims and asks to be hanged gets treated as a Yakuza-like suspect and deflected. Consider keeping the claim vague until a trial vote is in reach, and work the Village into a bloc that votes you out.

Track which Katana victims were protected: a repeated survival by the same claimed Medic plus a Sheriff's Not Evil on the Medic is weak evidence. Count the Yakuza's kill pattern (who they attack each night) to find the holder instead of trusting claims.

Treat alignment results as alignment clues, not role clears: a Not Evil result can fit a Katana holder, some Neutrals, or a framed player. State the exceptions when sharing results, and distinguish what you know from what you infer.

Read archive results according to their sampling rules. A partial, partly fake sample is not a census and cannot cap how many players may hold a role; use it as a clue, not proof against duplicate claims.

After a Yakuza flips, revisit the vote ledger. No votes on a nomination and Innocent votes at trial can be useful leads, but weigh whether those votes could actually have saved the player and combine them with other evidence.

Test the assumptions hidden in a player's argument. A conditional claim about what happens after an execution may reveal what they know—or may only be a bluff—so ask what facts would make the claim true before treating it as proof.

The Katana holder reads Not Evil to a Sheriff. On the night after a teammate is put on trial or publicly suspected, give the Katana to that teammate, since they are the player a Sheriff is most likely to check. An idle Grunt gains nothing by keeping it.
evidence: Bob was nominated by Heidi on Day 3, yet the Katana stayed with Erin on N3. Heidi checked Bob, got Evil, and he was hanged the next day. With the Katana, Bob would have read Not Evil.

tip: After a Katana attack fails, assume a Medic is involved. Kill the claimed protector, or use your disruption tools: a Smuggler swap can move the protection or the investigation. Retrying claimed investigators while holding swap tokens throws away nights.
evidence: Frank publicly claimed protecting Alice on Day 2, and the Yakuza attacked Heidi on N2 anyway; Frank had protected her. Bob died with both swap tokens unused, and Frank was only targeted on N4, after Bob was gone.

tip: When a teammate's hanging is clearly decided, vote Guilty with the majority. A lone Innocent vote saves nobody and becomes the first case against you once your teammate's role is revealed.
evidence: Bob was hanged 5-2 with Erin as the only other Innocent vote. On Day 5 Dave nominated Erin and cited exactly that vote.

tip: Never argue from game-end consequences that only a Yakuza could know, such as 'if I die, everyone left is Village.' Pitch to the Jester or other Neutrals with conditional reasoning that a villager could also say.
evidence: In her trial on Day 5, Erin told Grace that hanging her would leave only Village non-Jesters. Grace, Heidi, Alice and Dave all seized on the slip, and Erin was hanged.

tip: Don't let two teammates take the same safe claim, especially once an Archivist-type list is public. Three people claiming Vanilla with only one Vanilla in the list draws attention to exactly the right players.
evidence: Bob, Erin and Dave all claimed Vanilla against Carol's list, which showed one Vanilla. Carol's suspicion, though overstated, pointed at the two real Yakuza and got Bob onto Day 3's trial.

tip: Present an archive list as evidence that changes the odds, not as a count of every role. Say 'only 5 of 7 roles are sampled, so duplicate Vanilla claims are suspicious' rather than 'at least two must be lying.' Overstating it gets the point discredited even when the suspicion is correct.
evidence: Carol claimed the list proved two of the Vanilla claimers were lying, was rebutted by everyone, and retracted. Bob was acquitted 0-8 even though Bob and Erin were in fact the Yakuza.

tip: Once you have publicly claimed your protections, expect to become a target. Rotate protection, and spend a token on self-protection on the night your investigator's result has just exposed a Yakuza and you look like the next kill.
evidence: Frank announced his N1 and N2 protections, kept protecting Heidi every night, and died to the Katana on N4 with 2 medic tokens unused.

tip: Don't use up the Day's three trials on nominations nobody intends to vote Guilty on. Each 0-vote trial burns a nomination and reveals nothing new.
evidence: On Day 3, Bob, Carol and Frank were each tried and acquitted 0-8, ending the Day with no new information and no execution.
